sources.entry: Domoticz - Home Automation System that lets you monitor and configure various devices like: Lights, Switches, various sensors/meters like Temperature, Rain, Wind, UV, Electra, Gas, Water and much more. (Source Code, Clients) GPL-3.0 C/C++/Docker/Shell

summary.one_liner: Domoticz is a free, open source home automation system for monitoring and controlling lights, switches, and sensors such as temperature, rain, wind, UV, energy, gas, and water.
summary.what_it_does: Domoticz runs on Linux, Windows, macOS, FreeBSD, and Raspberry Pi or other ARM boards, and provides a web frontend that adapts to desktop and mobile browsers. The README says it supports 150+ hardware types, including Z-Wave, Zigbee, MQTT, RFXCOM, P1 Smart Meter, YouLess Meter, pulse counters, 1-Wire, and Philips Hue. Users can script events with dzVents (Lua) and Python plugins. It offers extended logging, push notifications to iPhone, Android, and desktop, auto-learning of sensors and switches, and manual creation of switch codes. External devices can be shared or used. On first run a setup wizard creates the admin account, and for Docker the DOMOTICZ_ADMIN_PASSWORD and DOMOTICZ_ADMIN_USERNAME environment variables can provision it automatically.
use_cases: monitor home temperature and energy meters
control lights and switches from a web browser
collect data from Z-Wave, Zigbee, or MQTT sensors
run home automation on a Raspberry Pi
send push notifications for home events
script home automation rules with Lua or Python
notable: Supports 150+ hardware types including Z-Wave, Zigbee, MQTT, and Philips Hue
Event scripting with dzVents (Lua) and Python plugins
Responsive HTML5 web frontend for desktop and mobile
Docker admin account provisioning through environment variables
Runs on Linux, Windows, macOS, FreeBSD, and ARM boards such as Raspberry Pi
caveats: The README says the GitHub issue tracker is not for end-user support; the Domoticz Forum is the first place to ask for help
The README does not include install or run commands; it links to external documentation for building from source
